# aircrack-ng

**Wi-Fi security auditing suite — capture, analysis and key recovery**

- **Version recorded:** 1.7
- **Categories:** `wifi`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.aircrack-ng.org/>

## What it does

A suite for auditing 802.11 networks: putting an adapter into monitor mode, capturing frames, and recovering WEP and WPA-PSK keys from captured handshakes offline.

## Why you would want it

It is the reference toolkit for wireless auditing and the one every piece of existing documentation assumes. The capture side is also generally useful for understanding what is on the air around you, independent of any key recovery.

## Before it will work

An adapter whose driver supports monitor mode and, for some tools, packet injection. Not every chipset does, and this is the single most common cause of 'it does not work'. airmon-ng will report which processes conflict.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`rf-security`](../profiles/rf-security.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install aircrack-ng --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `aircrack-ng`

## Known problems

NetworkManager and wpa_supplicant fight over an interface put into monitor mode; airmon-ng check kill is the usual answer, and it will drop your network connection. Key recovery against WPA depends on capturing a handshake, which requires a client to associate while you are listening.
